title: Strings
description: char arrays, string literals, and stdio

exercises.title: String Constants
exercises.description: Declare a string variable greeting and assign it the value "Hello, C!". Then print it using printf.
hints: `const char *greeting = "Hello, Go!";` — `puts(greeting);` matches the reference solution.

exercises.title: Using Runes
exercises.description: Declare a rune variable and assign it the Unicode character for 'A'. Print it using both %c and %d verbs to see character vs code point.

exercises.title: String Manipulation
exercises.description: Use strings.Contains to check if "Hello" is in "Hello, World!", strings.Replace to replace "World" with "C", and strings.Split to split "a,b,c" by comma.
exercises.expected_output:
Contains: true
Replaced: Hello, Go!
First: a
hints: Copy `text` to a writable `char buf[]`, locate `"World"` with `strstr`, patch to `Go!` and terminate like the sample.
`strtok` on `"a,b,c"` split by `","` to print the first token `a`.

exercises.title: String Formatting
exercises.description: Use print to format a string with a name and age, then print it. Also use print to format a floating point number to 2 decimal places.
exercises.expected_output:
Alice is 30 years old
Pi is 3.14
hints: `snprintf(line, sizeof line, "%s is %d years old", "Alice", 30);` then `puts(line);`

exercises.title: To Upper and To Lower
exercises.description: Given s = "C Programming", print it in all uppercase and then all lowercase.
hints: `strcpy` into `up`/`lo`, then loop bytes with `toupper` / `tolower` cast through `(unsigned char)`.

exercises.title: Reverse a String
exercises.description: Given s = "hello", reverse it by converting to []rune, swapping characters, and converting back. Print the reversed string.
hints: Mutable `char s[] = "hello";` — swap `s[i]` with `s[j]` for `i < j` moving inward.

exercises.title: String HasPrefix and HasSuffix
exercises.description: Declare url = "https://example.com". Check if it starts with "https://" and ends with ".com". Print both results.
